items.summary: Inflation is the general rise of prices over time, and it is measured, not guessed. After reading this you can read an inflation figure, tell a real wage from a nominal one, work out what inflation is really costing your household, and judge which savings protect you.
items.title: Inflation Explained: Why Everything Costs More

items.summary: Money at work has its own language, and most people learn it by accident. After reading this you can read a payslip, tell gross pay from net pay, compare two job offers properly, ask for a raise without guessing, and build a budget you can keep.
items.title: How to Talk About Salary and Expenses

items.summary: A boundary is a line you draw around your time, your body and your energy, said out loud so other people can respect it. After reading this you can say no to a request, a favour and a plan without damaging the relationship, hold a boundary when it is tested, and tell the difference between being polite and being pushed.
items.title: Setting Boundaries: How to Say No Politely

items.summary: Dating has a vocabulary of its own: a crush, a date, a situationship, ghosting, breadcrumbing. After reading this you know what each label means in practice, how to read a profile and a first message, what to say on a first date, how to ask about mixed signals, and how to end something without hurting anyone.
items.title: Understanding Modern Dating Expressions

items.summary: Disagreeing well is a skill with a shape: separate the idea from the person, acknowledge what is right before you object, and say the objection in plain words. After reading this you can disagree in a meeting, in a group chat and with someone more senior than you, and you can receive disagreement without taking it personally.
items.title: How to Disagree Without Being Rude

items.summary: Small talk is a skill with rules: how to open, how to keep a stranger talking, how to read the signs that it is working, and how to leave without an awkward goodbye. After reading this you can start a conversation with anyone in a queue, an office or a lift, and keep it going for five minutes without freezing.
items.title: The Art of Small Talk: Talking to Strangers Naturally

items.summary: Short videos and infinite feeds are engineered to hold your attention, and the result is a tired, scattered feeling after hours of scrolling. After reading this you can tell the difference between a weak attention span and a strong habit, spot the signs that the feed has taken over your day, and run a one-week reset that gives you your focus back.
items.title: Brain Rot: Is the Internet Destroying Our Attention Span?

items.summary: Scam messages are built on a small number of patterns, and those patterns leave signals you can learn to read in seconds. After reading this you can recognise the four structures behind almost every scam, spot the tells in a message before you act, run the first-ten-minutes procedure after an incident, choose payment methods that can be reversed, and say the sentences that stop a scammer without alarming the people around you.
items.title: How to Spot Online Scams and Fake Messages

items.summary: A hotel desk is a negotiation with rules you cannot see. After reading this you can read a booking, check in without queues, check the room in five minutes, ask for what you need, and leave without a surprise on the bill.
items.title: Checking Into a Hotel Like a Pro

items.summary: Every workplace has a layer of language that is not in the dictionary: phrases for a meeting, a delay, a mistake, a decision. After reading this you will understand the expressions you hear in offices, use them at the right moment, and avoid the ones that make you sound either too casual or too managerial.
items.title: Understanding Common Workplace Expressions

items.summary: One demo article: cover, stills, galleries, unique audio clips, unique videos, links, math, physics, chemistry, live graphs, and formulas — every locator is a real file in the zip.
items.title: Demo article with full assets

items.summary: Read ax + b = 0, keep both sides equal, and check the solution in English.
items.title: Solving a linear equation

items.summary: Working from another country is now possible for tens of millions of people, but it is governed by visa rules, tax rules and the cost of daily life. After reading this you can tell a genuine digital nomad from a tourist working online, check what you must do before you move, and pick a city that fits your work and your budget.
items.title: Digital Nomads: Working From Anywhere

items.summary: Moving to a new country changes small things before big ones: greetings, meals, punctuality, silence. After reading this you can name what is surprising you, tell a personal habit from a local rule, and handle the first weeks without assuming that your way is the correct one.
items.title: Culture Shock: Things That Surprise People Abroad

items.summary: People meet each other less than they did twenty years ago, and the reason is not that they stopped liking each other. After reading this you can explain the forces behind it, tell loneliness apart from solitude, plan shared time that people actually attend, and keep a friendship alive across distance and full calendars.
items.title: Why People Are Spending Less Time Together

items.summary: An anti-lock braking system is often taken as a promise that the car always stops in the same distance. It is not. After reading this you can describe how the system works, explain where it does not help, choose between threshold braking, progressive braking and engine braking, brake well with or without ABS, and say what to do when the warning light comes on.
items.title: ABS Is Not the Absolute Truth: The Limits of Anti-Lock Braking

items.summary: Washing machines, dishwashers and ovens are labelled in pictures so they can be used in any country. After reading this you can name the common symbols, choose the right programme and temperature, understand the salt, detergent and rinse aid symbols, and work a machine you have never used before.
items.title: Understanding Household Appliance Symbols

items.summary: A pump moves water, and a pump that moves water can also move current. After reading this article you can name the parts of a pump installation, explain where the leakage comes from, say how current reaches a person through wet ground, compare the six protections that guard the circuit, run a safe check on a pump, and give the right instructions in the first minutes after a shock.
items.title: Water Pumps and the Risk of Electric Leakage

items.summary: A water heater is a metal tank full of water with electricity inside it. After reading this article you can describe how a fault current reaches a person, name the parts that protect you, do the right things in the first minutes after a shock, describe the fault to a technician, and keep the appliance safe between services.
items.title: Water Heaters and the Electrocution Risk

items.summary: A medicine label tells you what is in the pack, how much is in one dose, and when to take it. After reading this you can read any medicine label in any country, measure a dose accurately, spot the instructions people most often ignore, and ask a pharmacist the questions that make the medicine work properly.
items.title: Understanding Medicine Labels and Dosage Instructions

items.summary: Doctors do not need more detail, they need better-arranged detail. After reading this you can describe a symptom so precisely that the doctor can narrow the cause quickly, answer the standard questions in full, and know when a symptom needs urgent care instead of a routine appointment.
items.title: How to Describe Symptoms to a Doctor

items.summary: Bảo walks into a green valley where dinosaurs still walk, and finds something small under a big leaf. Follow her past the ferns, the giant footprints and the warm nests. After reading, you can retell the journey, use five new dinosaur words in your own sentences, and explain why she left the bone in the ground.
items.title: A Journey Through Dinosaur Land

items.summary: A boy finds an old green door in the garden wall and opens it into a garden that should not exist. Follow him past the ivy, through the hidden garden and to the surprise waiting at the end. After reading, you can retell the adventure, use five new garden words in your own sentences, and explain why he keeps the door a secret.
items.title: The Secret Door in the Garden

items.summary: Tuấn finds an old map in his grandmother's attic and walks across the hill to look for buried treasure. Follow him through three clues, a compass with a shaky needle and a long afternoon of digging. After reading, you can retell the hunt, use five new explorer words in your own sentences, and say what the real treasure was.
items.title: The Little Explorer and the Hidden Treasure

items.summary: A girl climbs into a rocket and flies all the way to the Moon. Follow her through the countdown, the long dark sky and the quiet grey surface. After reading, you can retell the trip, use five new space words in your own sentences, and explain why the Moon feels light and bouncy.
items.title: A Trip to the Moon

items.summary: A small robot called Bit leaves the workshop to find a friend, and nothing goes the way it planned. Follow him through the street, the rain and the park at night. After reading, you can retell the adventure, use five new robot words in your own sentences, and explain how Bit finally made a friend.
items.title: The Robot Who Wanted a Friend

items.summary: A girl puts on her diving mask and swims down to the coral reef for the very first time. Follow her through the shallow water, the dark blue middle and the reef at the bottom. After reading, you can retell the adventure, use five new sea words in your own sentences, and explain why you should never touch a living coral.
items.title: My First Adventure Under the Sea

items.summary: Every animal has its own table, and its table decides where it lives and what it does. After reading this, you can sort animals into plant-eaters, meat-eaters and mixed-eaters, watch for the signs that tell you what an animal eats, and explain why plants and animals depend on each other.
items.title: What Do Animals Eat?

items.summary: A farm is a busy place where animals live, work and eat. After reading this you can name the animals you will meet on a farm, use the words farmers use every day, and visit a farm without frightening anybody.
items.title: Meet the Animals on the Farm

items.summary: Insects are small, but they are everywhere and they do enormous work. After reading this, you can spot an insect by its three body parts and six legs, learn what insects do for us, and watch them closely without hurting them.
items.title: The Wonderful World of Insects

items.summary: The ocean covers most of our planet, and every part of it is full of life. After reading this you can name the animals that live in each zone of the sea, use the words scientists use for them, and stay safe when you visit the beach.
items.title: Life Under the Ocean

items.summary: Your family is the people who belong with you. After reading this you can name the people in your family, say what each of them does, and introduce your family to somebody new.
items.title: Talking About Your Family

items.summary: A greeting is how a conversation starts. After reading this you can say hello to grown-ups and friends, say your own name, and start a small talk with anybody you meet.
items.title: Saying Hello and Introducing Yourself

items.summary: The weather is the easiest subject in the world to talk about, because everybody has one. After reading this you can describe the sky, tell how hot or cold it is, say what the weather is like, and choose the right clothes for the day.
items.title: Talking About the Weather

items.summary: A good friend listens, shares, tells the truth, and stays close. After reading this you can pick a good friend, be a good friend yourself, and fix a friendship after a quarrel.
items.title: What Makes a Good Friend?

items.summary: Asking for help is a skill, not a weakness. After reading this, you can try first, ask clearly, say what kind of help you need, and tell a grown-up straight away when something is really wrong.
items.title: How to Ask for Help

items.summary: Kindness is a set of small actions, not a special kind of person. After reading this, you can spot kindness in ordinary moments, welcome somebody who is left out, give a real compliment, and be kind to yourself on a hard day.
items.title: Being Kind to Others

items.summary: Everybody makes mistakes, and that is how people learn. After reading this you can spot a mistake, fix it, say sorry properly, and try again without feeling ashamed.
items.title: It's Okay to Make Mistakes

items.summary: Bread is flour and water and a tiny yeast. After reading this you can name the four ingredients, explain why bread rises, bake a simple loaf at home, and tell the difference between kinds of bread.
items.title: How Bread Is Made

items.summary: Breakfast is the first meal of the day. After reading this you can say what breakfast is for, name breakfasts from around the world, and make a simple breakfast for yourself at home.
items.title: What's for Breakfast?
